findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _tainted (`s["seq"] <= subject["seq"]` skips every earlier step, and the holder clause matches later steps only); README 'A gate's FAIL is never overridden' ('Counting forward from the subject'; 'An artefact that held the bytes before the subject is not covered either'); vectors.json V045
findings.finding:
Round 5 makes the failed artefact's own bytes forward-only too, not only the derived bytes. R4-1's option (a) kept the subject's own bytes on every holder. So a step that held the failed bytes before the gate's subject escapes the FAIL. That step, and anything that consumed it before the subject, can be delivered or consumed after the FAIL. Whether the bytes are decided depends only on which of two byte-identical steps the failing gate names. Accepted:
- A01: plan (bytes X) passes unit-tests; patch regenerates X and unit-tests FAILs it; plan is delivered. A01c, where the failing run names plan instead, is refused GATE_OVERRIDDEN.
- A02: patch passes schema-check; a read-back of patch returns X; unit-tests FAILs the read-back; patch is delivered. A02c, the FAIL on patch itself, is refused.
- A03: web-search returns X and passes schema-check; a second search returns the same X and unit-tests FAILs it; the non-idempotent post-ticket consumes the first search.
- A04: write-file applied plan (X) before patch (X) failed; a model step built on that write's result is delivered. Q04, the same with the write on patch, is refused.
- G02 (round-4 probe): a write consumes the earlier x after a FAIL on y with x's bytes. It was GATE_OVERRIDDEN in round 4 and under the round-4 sketch; it is now accepted.
- V045 pins the hole as a valid vector: plan passes schema-check only, a later byte-identical patch FAILs unit-tests, and plan is delivered.
The README's reason ('a gate's verdict can depend on the context it ran in') contradicts the contract's own interleaving rule ('A gate on the same bytes decides the same, so an earlier one counts'). A PASS on the same bytes counts at any time, while a FAIL counts only forward. That asymmetry fails open, and if context did matter, the later FAIL is the fresher verdict. The sibling ledger (MAS-RA-001 rule 4) makes any deterministic FAIL on the delivered quantity contradict it, whatever the order of checks (H13: a deterministic denial is not overridden). This partly reopens R1-1: the bytes a deterministic gate failed are delivered under another step, here an earlier one. The disposition cites S03c for the change, but S03c's coincident bytes are derived (a read of the patch), not the patch's own. The round-4 sketch accepts S03c and refuses G02.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _gated and _ungated (any passing gate counts); README 'Revisions', 'Deterministic gates interleave with model steps', 'Terminal status' (FAILED)
findings.finding: A revision needs only some passing gate before it is consumed or delivered, not the gate that failed its target. C03: unit-tests FAILs patch; r1 revises it and passes schema-check only. unit-tests never runs again, and r1 is delivered COMPLETED (accepted). C03b is the same under the strict profile (one round), also accepted. TR_FAILED shows the honest outcome when r1 is re-tested and fails (FAILED). A kernel avoids that status by not re-running the gate. HERMES re-executes and re-diagnoses every revised plan until it passes or the budget is spent (pp. 15, 20). HarnessDev's honest status reserves success for 'reasonable evidence that the final artifact completes the task' (p. 27). The FAIL is not overridden in bytes, but it is answered without evidence, and COMPLETED overstates. A fresh, undeclared attempt is a stated non-claim. The declared revision path is not covered by it.
findings.requiredChange: Before a revision's bytes reach a consumer or the delivery, require that every gate that failed a step of its revision chain has passed them: an OK run of that gateId on a holder of the revision's bytes. Pin C03 as a refusal, with a valid control where the revision passes the gate that failed. Or state it under 'Not claimed': the kernel chooses the gates, and a revision may be delivered after any one passing gate. Checked: a sketch of the rule in _gated, on top of the R5-1 sketch, keeps every vector's expectation (only V045 changes, from R5-1). It refuses C03 and C03b UNGATED_CONSUMPTION and changes no other probe of rounds 1 to 5.

findings.location: README 'A gate's FAIL is never overridden' ('so a tool output that merely repeats common bytes (an empty result, an acknowledgement) is not covered'); scripts/agent_loop.py _tainted (holder and copy clauses)
findings.finding:
The sentence holds for bytes derived from the artefact only. Two fail-closed reaches remain unstated, and each refuses a valid loop.
(1) The failed artefact's own bytes are matched in every later step, tool outputs included. So when the failed artefact is itself common bytes, every later tool output that repeats them is covered. D03: web-search returns '[]' and schema-check FAILs it. A local index read returns the same '[]', and a model step built on that read is refused GATE_OVERRIDDEN (D03b, with other bytes, is accepted). D02, where the failed '{}' is a model artefact, is refused UNGATED_CONSUMPTION, which is the interleaving rule's stated byte reach.
(2) A model step that repeats a derived output's short bytes is covered. D01: before unit-tests FAILs the gated patch, a judge model step returns 'approve' on it. After the revision passes, the same judge returns 'approve' on r1. A final step built on r1 and that verdict is refused GATE_OVERRIDDEN (D01b, with another verdict, is accepted).
findings.requiredChange: Say both reaches in the README beside that sentence, or narrow the sentence to derived bytes. Optionally advise that a judge's or check's output names its subject's digest, so equal verdicts on different subjects never share bytes.

findings.finding: _ungated calls _gated once per producer and consumer pair, and _gated recomputes _holders each time. Producers that share bytes share their consumers, so the check is cubic in steps. Measured: 100, 200 and 300 byte-identical model producers, each consumed by one write (201, 401 and 601 steps), take 0.09, 0.69 and 2.28 s. Extrapolated, not run: about 2,048 producers and 2,047 writes within the 4,096-step limit (about 3.6 MB) would take about 12 minutes. R4-2's path is now fine: 2,048 failing gates on one subject in 4,096 steps take 2.25 s.
findings.requiredChange: Index the steps by digest once, with the earliest OK gate per digest. Compute each digest's consumers once, not once per producer, so the check is near-linear. Optionally add a timing probe near the limit.

dispositions.evidence: The over-reach is resolved: _tainted is one forward pass, and derived bytes are matched only into MODEL and DELEGATE steps. Re-run: S01, S01c, S02, S03 and S03c are accepted (they were GATE_OVERRIDDEN in round 4). Their controls S01b, S01d, S02b, S03b and S03d stay accepted. Q08 and Q02 are refused and pinned by V137 and V138; V044 and V046 pin S01 and S02 as valid. But option (a) also required keeping 'the subject's own bytes on every holder as now', and round 5 does not. That opens R5-1: G02 is accepted, against the sketch's GATE_OVERRIDDEN, and V045 pins the hole as valid. V045 is not S03c's shape: it repeats the failed artefact's own bytes, not bytes derived from it.

The round-4 timing probe: 2,101 steps with 100 failing gates take 0.123 s (16.3 s in round 4). At the limit, 4,096 steps with 2,048 failing gates on one subject take 2.25 s. The pass runs once per failing gate, not once per distinct subject, but the bound is small. Another slow path remains (R5-4).

(1) The HOOK detail now exempts a HANDOFF-event hook ('only observes a loop that is already handing off'), and H03 is still accepted. (2) The README says the revision may consume all of it, and that a later round reads the previous round's artefact and diagnosis, not the original's. That matches HERMES p. 16 ('Previous Plan' and 'Diagnosis Feedback' from the previous iteration). S04, S04b and S04d keep their refusals, as now stated. (3) The depth mapping matches JAZ p. 7 n. 2 (top-level agent is depth 1) and pp. 16 and 18 (RecursionLimit(depth=1) disables subagents).

The round-3 probe re-run (Q01 to Q33) is identical to round 4. Only Q31's count of refusal cases changes (140 to 142, the two new refusal vectors). The round-4 controls H01 to H08, R01, R02, S04 to S10, G01, G03 and G04 keep their results.

_gated still has no producer lower bound: Q11 and Q11b are accepted, and V042 pins it. Its round-4 control G02 (a later FAIL on the same bytes) is now accepted; that regression is R5-1, not the gate-window defect.
The round-2 probes N01 to N31 give the same results as in round 4 (the output diff is empty apart from timings).

P01 (a fresh model step reproducing the failed digest, delivered) and P02 (a revision returning it) are still GATE_OVERRIDDEN. The earlier-step variant is reopened: A01, A02 and V045 deliver the failed bytes under an earlier step. Tracked as R5-1.

The round-1 probes P01 to P40, re-run through the round-2 script, give the same results as in round 4. That includes the agreement sweeps (P35 to P37: 0 disagreements), isolation (P38: 0 deviations), canonical agreement with MAS-RA-001 and -002 (P39: identical) and parse (P40).
